text:
Nikita Nesterenko sealed Friday's 5-3 win in Calgary with an empty-net goal, the Ducks' fourth straight win. It was his third goal of the season. He plays only 11 minutes a night, and lately less than 10.

Those minutes are worth more than they look. Anaheim takes 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Nesterenko at five on five, almost 15 points better than without him. He has 40 hits in 15 games and his individual chances (1.14 expected goals per 60 minutes) are better than you'd expect from a fourth-liner. His finishing is right on schedule.

Evolving-Hockey's small sample from last season agrees: 90th percentile at taking chances away, against competition in the 94th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (eight games) shows a dump-and-chase player, carrying the puck in on 28% of entries. He's 25, born in Brooklyn, a 2019 sixth-round pick of Minnesota who went through Boston College. We project about 12 goals. The thing we'd watch is whether the Ducks give him more than 10 minutes; his line keeps earning it.
headline: Nesterenko's quiet case
